sources.title: A nullable exclusion list
sources.text: For the three Item rows, WHERE price NOT IN (12, NULL) returns no rows. A match to 12 produces FALSE; an otherwise unmatched known price produces UNKNOWN because the list contains NULL. The missing price also produces UNKNOWN.

sources.title: A fixed three-row table
sources.text: The sandbox table Item(code, price, tag) contains exactly these rows: (A, 12, red), (B, 24, blue), and (C, NULL, red). NULL means a missing or unknown price. The notes do not explain why the price is missing.

sources.title: Comparison and filtering rules
sources.text: Ordinary comparisons involving NULL evaluate to UNKNOWN, including NULL = NULL. NOT UNKNOWN remains UNKNOWN. WHERE retains only TRUE and rejects FALSE and UNKNOWN. To include missing prices while excluding price 12, use price <> 12 OR price IS NULL.

sources.title: Aggregate rules
sources.text: COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(price) counts only non-NULL prices. SUM(price) adds the non-NULL prices and AVG(price) divides their sum by their count. For this Item table, COUNT(*) is 3, COUNT(price) is 2, SUM(price) is 36, and AVG(price) is 18.

sources.title: Order of join and filter operations
sources.text: A LEFT JOIN keeps unmatched left rows by padding right-side columns with NULL. A later WHERE right.active = 1 removes these unmatched rows. Putting right.active = 1 in the LEFT JOIN ON condition instead restricts matches while retaining every left row.
